# Sukhapatthanā Sutta (Iti 76 (It 3.27 PTS It 67))

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sukhapatthanā Sutta* ("Wishing for Happiness", Iti 76; It 3.27, PTS It 67) is a discourse in the *Itivuttaka* of the Khuddaka Nikāya. The core teaching urges that wise people who aspire to three forms of bliss should diligently guard their virtue. The discourse explains the three varieties of happiness that should be desired and warns against evil company and acquiring a bad reputation, illustrating through verse how associating with the wicked brings downfall [Anandajoti 2010].

  This poetic overlap is confirmed by DharmaNexus, which computes substantial text reuse between the verse section of Iti 76 (§4.4–9.6) and both Ja 503 (§23.1–27.6) and Ja 545 (§103.1–107.6), as well as corresponding segments in the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (Catuttho and Sattamo bhāgo) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also records smaller phrase alignments with prose discourses such as the *Gāmaṇi Saṁyutta* (SN 42), the *Apaṇṇaka Sutta* (MN 60), and fellow *Itivuttaka* suttas (Iti 66 and Iti 78) [DharmaNexus].

Selected verses from the discourse have also been anthologized and translated into English by Bhikkhu Ānandajoti [Anandajoti 2010].
